title: Hand-painted cake
subtitle: painting floral or botanical designs directly onto a fondant-covered cake with food colour
excerpt: A hand-painted cake uses gel food colours thinned with a clear spirit to paint designs directly onto a dry fondant surface. The fondant acts like paper, and the colours blend and layer in the same way as watercolour. Botanical florals, abstract washes, and detailed designs all work on this surface once the fondant is fully dry.
sourceNotes: Food-colour painting on fondant became a recognised cake decorating discipline in the 2010s, influenced by British decorators working in botanical and portrait styles and popularised through international competition coverage.

content.text: Painting on a fondant cake uses gel food colours thinned with vodka or clear spirit. The alcohol dries quickly and leaves no moisture on the surface, which matters because excess water softens fondant. The surface behaves like thick watercolour paper once the fondant has had 8 to 12 hours to dry. Colours layer and blend in the same way as paint.

Cover the cake in smooth, pale fondant. White or ivory gives the clearest results. Leave to dry at room temperature for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight. The surface should feel firm and slightly matt.

Mix the palette: put small amounts of gel food colour into a tile or plate. Add vodka drop by drop until the colour flows easily from the brush without running. Test on a piece of white fondant board before touching the cake.
Sketch the design lightly onto the cake surface with a food-safe pencil, or trace from a template held against the fondant.

Paint from background to foreground. Lay in pale washes first and let each layer dry for 5 minutes before adding darker detail on top. Colours blend wet-on-wet if worked quickly; they layer cleanly if the previous coat is dry.
Use a fine brush (size 1 or 2) for outlines and detail. Use a broader flat brush for washes. Clean between colours on a damp cloth.
Add gold or silver lustre dust at the end: mix with a tiny amount of spirit and apply with a dry brush. Let it dry for 2 minutes before handling.

attrs.problem: Colours bleeding or running on the surface
attrs.avoid: Avoid painting on fondant that has not fully dried; it absorbs liquid and the colour spreads.
attrs.fix: Give the covered cake a full 12 hours at room temperature before painting. If the fondant was refrigerated, let it come fully to room temperature and dry for an extra 2 hours before starting.

attrs.problem: Colour too transparent and barely visible
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-diluting the gel colour with too much spirit.
attrs.fix: Start with less spirit and build up gradually. Very deep, opaque colour needs barely any thinning at all.
